title: Functions, Pointers, and Ownership
summary: Define function contracts, pass values and addresses, use const pointers, validate null, and avoid dangling references.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Functions, Pointers, and Ownership
Compile and test behavior with warnings enabled
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: C passes arguments by value. To let a function modify a caller object, pass its address and dereference a validated pointer. A pointer stores an address; it is not an array length or ownership guarantee. Test against `NULL` before dereferencing when null is permitted. Use `const int *` when a function may read but not modify the pointed-to integer. Never return a pointer to an automatic local object because its lifetime ends when the function returns. Document who owns allocated memory and who must release it.
commonMistakes: mixing signed and unsigned values can distort comparisons
a successful run does not prove undefined behavior is safe
